## Variable Type → Description → Visualization → Test

| Variable Type | Summary | Graph | Common Bivariate Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nominal categorical | n (%) | Bar chart | Chi-square / Fisher's exact |
| Ordinal categorical | n (%), median rank | Bar chart | Chi-square (or trend test) |
| Continuous, normal | Mean ± SD | Histogram, box plot | t-test / ANOVA / Pearson r |
| Continuous, skewed | Median (IQR) | Histogram, box plot | Mann–Whitney / Kruskal–Wallis / Spearman |

## Common Regression Models

| Outcome | Model |
|---|---|
| Continuous | Linear regression |
| Binary | Binary logistic regression |

## Quick Contrasts

- **Mean ± SD vs Median (IQR):** use mean±SD only if roughly symmetric; skewed → median (IQR)
- **Chi-square vs Fisher's exact:** Fisher's when any expected cell count < 5
- **Independent vs paired t-test:** independent = different people; paired = same people, two time points/conditions
- **Pearson vs Spearman:** Pearson for linear, roughly normal continuous data; Spearman for monotonic/ordinal/non-normal data
- **95% CI:** range of plausible values for the true effect; excludes null (0 or 1) ↔ statistically significant
- **OR vs AOR:** COR = unadjusted; AOR = adjusted for confounders — always state the reference category

> Test selection also depends on your **study design and assumptions** — this sheet is a starting aid, not a substitute for understanding your data.
